verses.restored: In those days Hezekiah became sick to death. Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz came to him and said to him, Thus says YHWH: Command your house, for dying you shall die and not live.
He turned his face to wall and prayed to YHWH, saying,
Please, YHWH, remember how I walked before you in faithfulness and with whole heart and did what was good in your eyes. Hezekiah wept a great weeping.
Before Isaiah had gone out of middle court, word of YHWH came to him, saying,

Turn back and say to Hezekiah, leader of my people: Thus says YHWH, Divine of David your father: I heard your prayer; I saw your tears. Look, I am healing you. On third day you shall go up to house of YHWH.
I will add fifteen years to your days, and from hand of king of Assyria I will deliver you and this city. I will shield this city for my sake and for sake of David my servant.
Isaiah said, Take a cake of figs. They took and placed it upon boil, and he lived/recovered.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, What is sign that YHWH will heal me and I shall go up on third day to house of YHWH?
Isaiah said, This is sign for you from YHWH that YHWH will do word he spoke: Shall shadow go forward ten steps, or return ten steps?
Hezekiah said, It is easy for shadow to stretch ten steps; no, let shadow return backward ten steps.
Isaiah the prophet called to YHWH, and he brought shadow backward ten steps by which it had gone down on steps of Ahaz.
At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and gift to Hezekiah, for he heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

Hezekiah listened to them and showed them all house of his treasure: silver, gold, spices, good oil, house of weapons, and all found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them.
Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah and said to him, What did these men say, and from where did they come to you? Hezekiah said, From a distant land they came, from Babylon.
He said, What did they see in your house? Hezekiah said, All in my house they saw; there is nothing in my treasuries I did not show them.
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Hear word of YHWH.
Look, days are coming when all in your house and what your fathers stored until this day shall be carried to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says YHWH.
From your sons who come from you, whom you father, they shall take, and they shall be eunuchs/court officials in palace of king of Babylon.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, Good is word of YHWH you spoke. He said, Is it not so, if peace and truth are in my days?
Remaining acts of Hezekiah, all his might, how he made pool and conduit and brought water into city, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
Hezekiah lay with his fathers, and Manasseh his son became king in his place.

translation_notes: A prophetic declaration of death is reversed before Isaiah leaves the court. This chapter itself rejects treating a prognosis or claimed revelation as beyond review, prayer, new information, or change.
Hezekiah's tears are not lack of faith. Serious illness, anticipatory grief, and fear of death deserve presence and care.
The story does not promise that sincere prayer will add fifteen years to every life. People who die, remain ill, or receive no reversal have not prayed incorrectly.
The fig cake/poultice is an ancient treatment detail and not a substitute for diagnosis, emergency care, antibiotics, surgery, oncology, or evidence-based medicine.
The shadow sign is narrated as wonder. It must not be used as a modern astronomical claim or a test believers must reproduce.
Hezekiah shows Babylonian envoys wealth, spices, oil, weapons, and defenses. Hospitality and diplomacy do not require exposing every vulnerable resource.

The prediction of Babylonian plunder and deportation shifts consequences onto future generations. It must not justify collective punishment or teach that descendants deserve disaster for an ancestor's pride.

The Hebrew sarisim can refer to eunuchs or court officials. Eunuch identity is not shame, emasculation rhetoric, or evidence of reduced human worth; forced bodily alteration under empire would be violence.
Hezekiah's relief that peace will last in his days reveals a dangerous short horizon. Leadership must include consequences beyond one's own lifetime.
The pool and conduit honor public infrastructure that preserves life during siege; engineering and communal planning are part of the king's legacy.
safety_note: Do not turn Hezekiah's healing into a guarantee, reject medical care, shame those who die, treat a prophet's first word as infallible, stigmatize eunuchs, or excuse future deportation as a descendant's punishment. Preserve grief, changing prognosis, practical treatment, infrastructure, and responsibility to generations beyond one's own peace.
